exposure: Bariatric surgery (specifically, between a first and second pregnancy)
outcome: Admission of infants to a special care nursery or neonatal intensive care
cohort: The study included all women aged 15-45 years with a hospital record in New South Wales (NSW), Australia (2002-2014), and all women giving birth in NSW (1994-2015), totaling 1,606,737 women.
finding: Bariatric surgery performed between a first and second pregnancy was associated with reductions in obesity-related adverse pregnancy outcomes, including hypertension, spontaneous preterm birth, and infants large for gestational age, in the subsequent pregnancy.
followup_time: Outcomes were assessed in a subsequent pregnancy after bariatric surgery, within a data collection period for births spanning 1994-2015.
